body:
## Person decision 2026-11-17: mocked native runs, Full control enabled (revision 4 adopted)

The orchestrator explained why Windows Hello guards protected decisions, and the risk of mocking it: the security boundary goes unproved on a real machine. The person then chose:

- Mock every native, OS and model run in this epic.
- Ship Full control enabled, with no feature flag.
- Run the live native test themselves after merging to main and installing the update. A failure there is handled by a patch fix or a revert.

Windows Hello is not available on this machine. The person allowed a test VM and asked that it be cleaned up afterwards. None was set up: Hyper-V, Windows Sandbox and VirtualMachinePlatform are not installed, enabling them needs an admin prompt and a reboot, and the reboot would end the run. Once the runs are mocked, no VM is needed.

Saved revision 4 (rv_01m7mn04h1br1rt2tj2zhnmkx7) was adopted at a paused point with no open attempts. Seventeen run-only tickets now run their accepted case once, in-process, against fake ports. Their evidence is labelled NONHUMAN / NOT NATIVE-PROVEN and is never reported as native success. At runtime, protected decisions still route to Windows Hello and are denied when Hello is unavailable.
